notes: Creates Gh29105Tests, a test whose two nested @Configuration classes each declare a @Bean method annotated with Spring's org.springframework.core.annotation.Order (@Order(-1) on customService, @Order(0) on defaultService), and asserts that a child context returns the beans in that order. The @Order here is Spring's bean ordering, imported by a single type import, not JUnit Jupiter's org.junit.jupiter.api.Order, and it sits on a @Bean factory method, not on a test method or a test class, so it pins no test order. ADR 0007 Decision 6 rejects @Order only when it resolves to org.junit.jupiter.api.Order and is placed on a method or a class that runs tests; the checker must accept this with no code. It is not a flaky test fix; it is the regression test of a Spring Framework bug fix (gh-29105). Verbatim: only the new test file of the commit is kept; the production change to DefaultListableBeanFactory.java, the other test change and the index line are dropped. No pull request: the commit closes issue gh-29105 directly. Not from IDoFT: the repository does not appear in pr-data.csv under any status.
